q: Choose the correct preposition: "The museum has been closed for renovation ________ Monday last."
e: "Since" is used with a definite starting point in time ("Monday last", "2015", "morning") in Perfect/Perfect Continuous tenses. "For" is used with a period/duration of time.

q: Fill in the blank: "The ancestral property was divided equally ________ the two brothers."
e: "Between" is used for two persons or things (or distinct individual relationships), whereas "among" is used for more than two considered collectively.

q: Select the correct pair of prepositions: "The venomous snake was killed ________ the farmer ________ a heavy bamboo stick."
e: In passive constructions, "by" introduces the living agent/doer ("the farmer"), while "with" introduces the physical instrument/tool used ("a heavy bamboo stick").

q: Fill in the blank: "Seeing the drowning child, the lifeguard immediately dived ________ the river."
e: "Into" expresses movement from outside to inside (motion + change of location), whereas "in" indicates static position inside an enclosed space.

q: Choose the correct set of prepositions: "The ceremony begins ________ 10:30 a.m. ________ Saturday ________ December."
e: Standard time preposition hierarchy: "at" for exact clock time ("at 10:30 a.m."), "on" for specific days/dates ("on Saturday"), and "in" for months, seasons, and years ("in December").

q: Complete the sentence: "Most readers prefer classical poetry ________ modern free verse."
e: "Prefer" (and Latin comparatives like "senior", "junior", "superior", "inferior", "prior") always takes the preposition "to", never "than".

q: Fill in the blank: "Though she is fond ________ classical music, she is afraid ________ performing on stage."
e: Both adjectives "fond" and "afraid" take the fixed preposition "of" ("fond of", "afraid of"). Using "from" after "afraid" is a common error.

q: Choose the correct preposition: "Come and sit ________ me so that we can share the textbook."
e: "Beside" means "by the side of / next to", whereas "besides" means "in addition to / apart from".

q: Select the correct pair: "Rohan is exceptionally good ________ trigonometry, though slightly weak ________ spelling."
e: Proficiency or skill in an activity/subject takes "good/bad/clever + at", whereas deficiency in a subject takes "weak + in".

q: Complete the sentence: "The entire faculty congratulated her ________ her brilliant success in the TGT examination."
e: The verb "congratulate" strictly takes the preposition "on" ("congratulate someone on something"), never "for".

q: Fill in the blank: "Please submit your revised synopsis ________ Friday evening at the latest."
e: "By" indicates a deadline ("not later than Friday evening"), whereas "until/till" denotes continuous duration up to a point in time ("stay until Friday").

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb meaning "to take care of": "Who will ________ your elderly parents while you are abroad?"
e: "Look after" means to take care of. Distractors: "look into" (investigate), "look for" (search for), "look up" (consult a reference/improve).

q: Select the correct phrasal verb meaning "to abandon a habit": "On his doctor's advice, he finally decided to ________ smoking."
e: "Give up" means to quit or abandon. Distractors: "give in" (surrender/yield), "give away" (distribute/betray a secret), "give out" (emit/become exhausted).

q: Choose the correct preposition: "Thousands of people died ________ cholera during the nineteenth-century epidemic."
e: "Die of" is used for diseases, hunger, thirst, or grief ("die of cholera/cancer"), whereas "die from" is used for external causes like wounds, overwork, or snakebite.

q: Identify the grammatically CORRECT sentence:
o: We discussed about the new syllabus thoroughly.
She entered into the auditorium quietly.
The police are investigating the theft carefully.
He resembles with his elder brother.
e: Transitive verbs like "discuss", "enter" (physical space), "investigate", and "resemble" take a direct object WITHOUT a preposition. Only C is error-free.

q: Fill in the blank: "During the austerity drive, citizens were urged to abstain ________ wasteful expenditure."
e: Verbs of avoidance and restraint—such as "abstain from", "refrain from", "desist from", and "prohibit from"—always take "from".

q: Choose the correct pair of prepositions: "The management refused to accede ________ our demands unless we complied ________ the new code."
e: "Accede" (agree/consent) always takes "to", while "comply" (obey rules) always takes "with" ("abide by" takes "by").

q: Select the correct preposition: "For want of reliable evidence, the sessions court acquitted the accused ________ all charges."
e: Legal verbs of judgment—"acquit of", "convict of", "accuse of", and "guilty of"—take the fixed preposition "of" (never "from").

q: Complete the sentence: "A true scholar is never averse ________ constructive criticism."
e: The adjective "averse" (strongly disinclined/opposed) always takes "to" ("averse to risk/criticism"), just like "opposed to" and "indifferent to".

q: Choose the correct pair of prepositions: "The old watchmaker is blind ________ his left eye, yet the landlord remains blind ________ his plight."
e: "Blind in" refers to physical blindness in a specific eye ("blind in one eye"), whereas "blind to" means figuratively ignoring or failing to notice faults or suffering ("blind to his plight").

q: Fill in the blanks accurately: "While his grandfather died ________ pneumonia, his uncle died ________ overwork and exhaustion."
e: Direct internal illness/disease takes "die of" ("died of pneumonia"), while an indirect/external cause such as overwork, wounds, or food poisoning takes "die from".

q: Select the correct pair: "This wholesale merchant deals ________ silk fabrics and knows how to deal ________ difficult clients."
e: "Deal in" means to trade or do business in a commodity ("deals in silk"), whereas "deal with" means to handle a person, problem, or topic.

q: Complete the sentence: "I cannot agree ________ you on this point, nor can I agree ________ such an unfair proposal."
e: "Agree with" is used for a person ("agree with you"), "agree to" is used for a proposal/plan/terms, and "agree on/about" is used for a matter or point of discussion.

q: Choose the correct pair of phrasal verbs: "The firefighters managed to ________ the blaze before the committee decided to ________ the inauguration."
e: "Put out" means to extinguish fire/lights; "put off" means to postpone. ("Put by" = save money; "put up with" = tolerate.)

q: Fill in the blank: "The workers' union decided to ________ the strike after the minister assured a fair wage revision."
e: "Call off" means to cancel. Distractors: "call on" (visit a person), "call for" (demand/require), "call up" (telephone/summon for military duty).

q: Select the correct phrasal verb: "Shortly after the monsoon floods, a severe epidemic of malaria ________ in the low-lying villages."
e: "Break out" means to start suddenly (used for wars, fires, epidemics). Distractors: "break into" (enter forcibly), "break down" (fail mechanically/emotionally), "break up" (disperse/end a relationship).

q: Complete the sentence: "His speech was completely devoid ________ humour and deprived the audience ________ any real inspiration."
e: Both "devoid of" (completely lacking) and "deprive someone of" (take away) strictly require the preposition "of".

q: Choose the correct pair: "This antique table is made ________ Burma teak, whereas fine wine is made ________ fermented grapes."
e: "Made of" is used when the original material remains physically recognizable (wood → table), whereas "made from" is used when the raw material undergoes a chemical/structural transformation (grapes → wine, milk → cheese).

q: Fill in the blank: "Because the ambulance reached the hospital just ________, the patient's life was saved."
e: "In time" means early enough before it is too late (for a crisis/opportunity), whereas "on time" means punctually according to a fixed timetable ("The train arrived on time").

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb meaning "to reject an offer": "Despite the lucrative salary, she ________ the offer to stay near her family."
e: "Turn down" means to reject/refuse (or lower volume). Distractors: "turn up" (appear/arrive), "turn out" (prove to be/attend), "turn over" (hand over/capsize).

q: Fill in the blank: "With persistent diplomacy, the elder brother prevailed ________ him to withdraw the lawsuit."
e: "Prevail upon/on" means to persuade someone successfully, whereas "prevail over/against" means to triumph or defeat an opponent.

q: Select the correct phrasal verb: "The forensic report completely ________ the eyewitness's testimony."
e: "Bear out" means to confirm or corroborate evidence. Distractors: "bear with" (be patient with), "bear away" (win a prize), "bear down" (crush/overpower).

q: Complete the sentence: "The region is richly endowed ________ fertile alluvial soil, though the old granary was infested ________ rodents."
e: Both "endowed with" (naturally blessed with) and "infested with" (overrun by pests) take the fixed preposition "with".

q: Choose the correct pair: "The impoverished collector could not bear to part ________ his rare folio, nor could he part ________ his loyal assistant."
e: "Part with" is used for relinquishing a thing/possession ("part with his rare folio"), whereas "part from" is used for separating from a person ("part from his loyal assistant").

q: Fill in the blank: "In the dense December fog, the pilot could barely ________ the runway lights."
e: "Make out" means to discern, decipher, or understand with effort. Distractors: "make up" (invent/reconcile), "make for" (head towards/contribute to), "make over" (transfer property/renovate).

q: Choose the precise preposition: "A conscientious magistrate must never connive ________ corruption in his own office."
e: "Connive at" (like "wink at") means to deliberately ignore or tacitly allow a wrongdoing. ("Connive with" is used before a person—to conspire with someone.)

q: Select the correct pair of prepositions: "Having grown inured ________ hardship, the veteran was still amenable ________ reasoned counsel."
e: Both "inured to" (hardened/accustomed to something unpleasant) and "amenable to" (responsive/open to) strictly take the preposition "to".

q: Choose the accurate pair: "While his prose style differs markedly ________ Hardy's, I respectfully differ ________ the critic on his conclusion."
e: "Differ from" indicates dissimilarity between things or people ("differs from Hardy's"), whereas "differ with" means to disagree in opinion with a person ("differ with the critic").

q: Fill in the blank: "Everyone in the hall was completely ________ by the speaker's sudden resignation."
e: "Taken aback" (always passive) means shocked or startled. Distractors: "taken in" (deceived), "take after" (resemble an elder relative), "take over" (assume control).

q: Complete the sentence: "The villagers remonstrated ________ the contractor ________ the substandard road material."
e: Standard formal usage is "remonstrate with (a person) against/about (a thing/action)" meaning to protest forcefully in reasoned objection.

q: Choose the correct phrasal verb meaning "to fail or come to nothing": "Due to a sudden lack of funding, the ambitious heritage project ________."
e: "Fall through" means to collapse or fail to materialize (for plans/deals). Distractors: "fall out" (quarrel), "fall back" (retreat), "fall in" (collapse inward/line up).

q: Fill in the blank: "In the royal banquet hall, dozens of liveried attendants waited ________ the visiting dignitaries."
e: "Wait on/upon" means to attend to or serve someone (especially at table or formally), whereas "wait for" means to stay expecting someone's arrival.

q: Identify the sentence that uses a prepositional phrase INCORRECTLY:
o: The appeal was dismissed in accordance with Section 14.
He resigned in consequence of failing health.
She spoke with a view to persuade the reluctant jury.
The troops marched in spite of the torrential downpour.
e: In "with a view to", "to" is a preposition (NOT an infinitive marker) and must be followed by a gerund ("with a view to persuading"), making C grammatically incorrect.

q: Select the correct pair: "Once winter ________ early in November, the mountaineers immediately ________ reinforcing their base camp."
e: "Set in" means to begin and seem likely to continue (used for seasons/weather/decay), while "set about" means to start tackling a task energetically.

q: Choose the correct pair of prepositions: "The headmaster was deeply vexed ________ the clerk ________ his chronic negligence."
e: Like "angry/annoyed", "vexed" takes "with" before a person ("vexed with the clerk") and "at" before a thing, conduct, or event ("at his chronic negligence").

q: Choose the correct pair of phrasal verbs: "The new education policy aims to ________ structural reform, though it took hours to ________ the dissenting members."
e: "Bring about" means to cause to happen; "bring round" means to persuade someone to change their mind (or restore consciousness). ("Bring off" = succeed in a difficult feat.)

q: Fill in the blanks: "Modern digital offices have largely dispensed ________ carbon paper and disposed ________ bulky filing cabinets."
e: "Dispense with" means to do without/eliminate as unnecessary, whereas "dispose of" (single 'f', never 'off') means to get rid of or sell.

q: Select the phrasal verb meaning "to abolish completely": "Social reformers fought relentlessly to ________ outdated discriminatory customs."
e: "Do away with" means to abolish or eradicate. Distractors: "do up" (renovate/fasten), "do over" (redo), "do someone out of" (cheat someone out of).

q: Complete the sentence: "Such evasive silence is tantamount ________ an admission of guilt and is scarcely compatible ________ judicial integrity."
e: "Tantamount" (equivalent in effect) always takes "to", and "compatible" (able to coexist harmoniously) always takes "with".

q: Identify the ONLY grammatically flawless sentence among the following:
o: The new anthology comprises of twenty-five Victorian poems.
She struggled bravely to cope up with the mounting workload.
The committee ordered for a fresh inquiry into the discrepancy.
The anthology comprises twenty-five Victorian poems.
e: In active voice, "comprise" means "consist of" and NEVER takes "of" ("be comprised of" is passive). Likewise, "cope with" never takes "up", and transitive "order" never takes "for". Only D is completely correct.
